solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Meat firm lies about antelope

indicators.note: the firm wraps itself around the meat, sitting on either side of it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
ham is a cured meat
as in 'the answer lies here' = 'the answer is here'

explanation.surface: A butcher's business is caught out being dishonest about its antelope meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies' looks like dishonesty, but it is the verb of position: where something lies is where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The chamois is a goat-like mountain animal of the Alps, classed among the goat-antelopes.

clue.text: They've gone off after a match official

definitions.text: They've gone off after a match official

parts.words: They've gone off after a match official
parts.note: surface reading: players leaving the pitch after a game, or people chasing a referee
setter's reading: a match is a marriage, and once it is made official the newlyweds go away on holiday together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match official' looks like a referee, but read 'official' as an adjective: the match (the wedding) has been made official.
explanation.definitionFit: Newlyweds leave for a holiday right after the wedding ceremony, so they have literally gone off after the union.

clue.text: Great leader one's taken bananas on hospital visits

indicators.note: 'one's taken on' means the single letter is added to the end
a visitor goes inside, so the hospital letter is placed within the madness word

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A notable leader takes a bunch of bananas along when visiting someone in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: MAD with H inside gives MAHD, and I is added: MAHDI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic belief the Mahdi is the prophesied redeemer and guide who will appear before the end of days.

clue.text: Changing sides on one occasion, guerrilla shot soldier

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
changing sides means swapping left for right, so one letter standing for a side is exchanged
only once: just a single instance is swapped, not every one

parts.note: taken as written; it has two Ls, one of which is swapped
of the two sides, left L and right R, the right one is brought in

explanation.surface: A guerrilla fighter switches allegiance once and shoots a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap one L (left) for R (right) in GUERRILLA, then rearrange to IRREGULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular is a fighter outside a regular army, such as a militia member or partisan.

clue.text: Immediately punched by distinguished companion (others too)

indicators.note: a punch goes into something, so the honour letters are driven inside the word for immediately

parts.note: anon is an old word for at once
a Companion of the Distinguished Service Order puts DSO after their name

explanation.surface: Someone is punched straight away by a celebrated companion, and other people get the same treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The DSO is a British military decoration for distinguished service; its holders are called Companions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase ends a list to mean that further similar items follow, the way etcetera does.

clue.text: Hooter's out of action, as always

definitions.note: possessive noun read as the adjective 'of the nose'

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows, ignoring the gaps

parts.note: letters drawn from the end of the first word through the second into the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone's car horn, or perhaps their nose, is broken yet again, as it always is.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooter is British slang for a nose (and also a car horn), so 'hooter's' means belonging to the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal is the adjective for anything relating to the nose, the body part a hooter jokingly names.

clue.text: Husband returning home with both sons bears public examination

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece bears another by sitting on top of it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
H is the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the words for home and both are read from right to left

parts.note: a lair is an animal's home
both means the two of them

explanation.surface: A father comes home with his two sons, who are carrying something to show the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the home and both words turn round; the son and husband letters stay put, the son sitting on top in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A show trial is a staged court case held in public for propaganda, its verdict decided in advance.

clue.text: Now excluded, like actor sacked on set?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: no longer involved or considered
second meaning, playful: a performer fired during filming is literally removed from the film

explanation.surface: An actor is fired mid-shoot and finds himself left out of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means no longer involved, and a sacked film actor is no longer in the movie being made.

clue.text: Rotting oak, nutwood and why this might be a surprise…

indicators.note: rotting material breaks down and falls apart, so these letters are reformed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds decaying oak and nut timber and wonders why, which comes as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation used to announce something unexpected, so it typically precedes a surprising remark.

clue.text: Brigade's juniors, some section embracing church sphere with love

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms round, so the outer word encloses the inner pieces

parts.note: as in 'have you got some/any?'
CH is the abbreviation for church
an orb is a globe or sphere
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
S is an abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: Part of a youth brigade includes a church group and a spirit of love.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boys' Brigade is a Christian youth organisation in the UK and Ireland; 'some section' supplies the outer letters around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchor Boys is the name of the youngest age section of the Boys' Brigade, for small children.

clue.text: Hate being out of bounds? You shouldn't lie on it

indicators.note: with its bounds out, the word loses the letters at both of its edges

parts.note: to loathe is to hate

explanation.surface: Hatred is forbidden, a moral principle you ought not to break.
explanation.walkthrough: LOATHE loses its first and last letters to give OATH; 'lie on it' puns on lying while under oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given under a sworn promise must be truthful, so lying there is perjury.

clue.text: Cake-decorating gadget Spooner's given key workers

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial consonants of two words trade places

parts.note: a nozzle tool that pipes icing onto cakes; swapping the P and T sounds gives the answer

explanation.surface: A baker's icing gadget is handed over to essential staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key workers' sounds like essential staff, but here they are people who press keys all day.
explanation.definitionFit: A typing pool was an office team of typists, workers whose job was striking keyboard keys.

clue.text: Old President Trump cultivating a smaller behind

indicators.note: growing a different, smaller one means the existing word for the backside is swapped for a shorter word

parts.note: taken as written; it ends in RUMP, a word for the behind
aft means behind or at the back, and is shorter than RUMP

explanation.surface: A jibe that Donald Trump is trying to slim down his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUMP is T + RUMP; replace that rump with the smaller word AFT.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th President of the United States, serving from 1909 to 1913.

clue.text: Date… fancy… get off… fall asleep

parts.note: to go out with someone is to date them
to fancy someone is to like them
to alight is to get off a bus or train

explanation.surface: A dating story in fragments: a date, attraction, getting off with someone, then nodding off.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, to get off with someone is to kiss them, so the surface tells a romance; here it means leaving a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes dropping off to sleep very quickly and completely, like a lamp switched off.

clue.text: Face showing such a scarlet shade after nun and VIP discovered together

indicators.note: the phrase for so scarlet is placed after the uncovered pair
joined up and then uncovered, the combined word loses its outermost letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
so means to such a degree
scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A nun and a celebrity are caught together, their faces blushing a deep scarlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Together' joins nun and VIP into one string first, so only its very first and very last letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor covers the face, so a knight without one has an exposed face that can be seen.

clue.text: Riotous behaviour increases after arresting European cohorts

indicators.note: the word for increases follows the container
to arrest is to take into custody, so the riot word holds the single letter inside

parts.note: aggro is British slang for aggressive, rowdy behaviour
E is the abbreviation for European
ups are rises, as in ups and downs

explanation.surface: Rising disorder follows the arrest of a European with his band of followers.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggro is British slang, short for aggravation, meaning trouble or fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort is a group of people sharing a characteristic, especially those born in the same period.

clue.text: Widely talked about score-draw punctuated by extremely careless errors

indicators.note: something punctuated is broken into by an insertion, so the extreme word is placed in the middle of the draw

parts.note: a score-draw is a drawn match with goals, such as one-one
very means extremely
slips are small careless mistakes

explanation.surface: A football match ends level after a string of careless defensive blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: A score-draw is the British football pools term for a draw in which goals were scored, so one-one fits.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is being mentioned by everyone, it is a common topic of conversation.

clue.text: Stud manager

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a round raised knob or stud on a surface, such as on a shield
second meaning: the person in charge at work

explanation.surface: The person who runs a horse-breeding farm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an ornamental raised knob, like a stud, and the person in charge of others at work.

clue.text: Large building vehicle pulling barrels forward

parts.note: a tower is a vehicle that tows another
B is used as an abbreviation for barrels
a lock is a forward position in rugby

explanation.surface: A truck tows a load of barrels ahead of it.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union, the locks are second-row forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower block is a tall multi-storey building, usually of flats or offices.

clue.text: Appetising as the brown bread out of the top of oven

indicators.note: taking that letter out of the toast word removes it

parts.note: browned bread is toast, so like it is toasty

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of oven

explanation.surface: Bread browned in the oven smells delicious as it comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: TOASTY with O removed gives TASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tasty has a pleasant flavour, so it is appealing to eat.

clue.text: One breaks down only single beds

indicators.note: a bed holds something within it, so the answer is embedded in the words

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Somebody collapses at the sight of single beds only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One breaks down' looks like a person in tears; it means a substance that breaks cells down.
explanation.definitionFit: A lysin is an antibody or other agent that causes cells to dissolve and rupture.

clue.text: Heartless sister keeps dad in box

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the outer letters hold the father word inside
without its heart the word keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters of sister
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: An unkind sister shuts their father in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In box' looks like a container signal, but 'in' is a link and 'box' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice, throwing punches without full force.

clue.text: Dignified cycling a post-Monday pursuit

indicators.note: going round in a cycle moves letters from the end back to the front

parts.note: taken as written
Tues is the abbreviation for Tuesday, the day after Monday
a quest is a search or pursuit

explanation.surface: Riding a bike is a refined activity for the start of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: ATUESQUEST has its last two letters moved to the front: ST + ATUESQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuesque describes someone tall, graceful and stately, like a statue in bearing.

clue.text: I won't miss cases of disease and — especially — onset of epidemic

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so only the outer letters of each word are kept

parts.note: outer letters of disease

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: outer letters of and
outer letters of especially
the opening letter of epidemic

explanation.surface: A doctor counts cases of a disease, especially at the start of an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases of' applies to all three words in the list: DE, AD, EY, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadeye is an expert marksman, someone who boasts that every shot hits its target.

clue.text: In two, like 2?

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
the entry at 2 is a pair who went off, here read as gone under

explanation.surface: A pair split apart, just like the newlyweds clued at 2 down?
explanation.walkthrough: The wedding service says 'let no man put asunder', which is what the honeymooners of 2 down hope never happens; the question mark flags the irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn asunder means split into separate parts, so something asunder is broken into two pieces.
